gaps.sentence: He always ___ the truth, however unpleasant it is.
gaps.explanation: tell the truth is the fixed collocation; 'say the truth' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: We ___ a taxi from the airport because it was raining.
gaps.explanation: take a taxi/bus/train is the standard collocation for using transport.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ a decision next week.
gaps.explanation: make a decision is the fixed collocation; we do not 'do' or 'give' a decision.

gaps.sentence: The new evidence has ___ doubt on the original conviction.
gaps.explanation: 'Throw doubt on' is the fixed phrase for casting suspicion on something.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: Unlike some politicians, she ___ her promises.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'promises' (she is unlike other politicians)
gaps.explanation: keep a promise means to do what you promised; the contrast with other politicians shows the positive verb.

gaps.sentence: I would never ___ advice from someone I don't respect.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'advice' from the receiver's side
gaps.explanation: take advice from somebody means to accept and follow it; the adviser gives advice.
